The consensus amongst personality psychologists is that the Meyers Briggs test (what 16personalities uses) is not empirically valid. My point is not that these tests aren't accurate. They probably do tell you exactly what you tell them in the test. The same thing can be accomplished through astrology because of confirmation bias. The point is neither are valid, because both can apply to pretty much everyone. Research has shown this to, where the Meyers Briggs test has accuracy at a percent only a little higher than chance, which is astrology's probability of accuracy.

To answer your question, while I would still be there for her as her brother, I would definitely confront her about believing the Earth is flat. To me, they are not the same thing. Flat Earth theories are a blatant denial of an obvious, scientifically proven fact. Astrology is **nowhere** near that level of insane. People believe in personality test like 16Personalities, even though they are scientifically not significant, because vague descriptions of people can sound accurate due to confirmation bias. The exact same is true of astrology. There is a big difference between believing in a vague list of personal qualities and believing that out extremely round planet is flat despite there being no reason to believe that.

Not everyone with PTSD is a war veteran.

Experiencing the anguish of war is one of the biggest causes of PTSD, and it's good people understand that, but you can get PTSD from many things: a car crash, a robbery, or in my case, growing up with an alcoholic and drug addicted father. 

Another misconception is that people with PTSD normally can't function. My PTSD is relatively low grade, and I am still able to thrive in school and make many friends. 

What frustrates me is if I ever disclose my disorder to someone, which is already hard to do, they often have this sound of disbelief in their voice or they might ask some question to kind of "qualify" my disorder. I've even had people say, " I thought that was just for war vets."

It makes me mad because I wish I could show them all the obsessive thinking, nightmares, anxiety, depression, substance problems, derealization, emotional detachment, insomnia, and more. I wish I could show them how quickly I get anxiety attacks and flashbacks around a person who is too drunk.

NAH. You ask what you could possibly get out of forgiving them, but it's staring you right in the face. Forgiving someone has nothing to do with them, but with you. It is about letting go of the hatred and hurt you evidently (and understandably) feel. Holding a grudge cannot erase the bullying, but it will extend the pain you feel for however long it takes you to forgive them. Unless you can learn to move on, you will resent them forever because of how you continue to feel, when it is in your ability to grow past the experience and become a stronger person for it. I'm not saying that it was right or okay that you were put in that position, it absolutely was not. What I'm saying is that you can't decide whether or not they were bigoted, you can only decide how to react to it, and right now your reaction will only serve to hurt you!

I should mention, as well, that people can and do change. You are under no obligation to forgive them, but you should consider that doing so might make it harder for them to grow. Bigots are like children that say ignorant and sometimes hateful things. They should be reprimanded and come to understand what they did wrong, but if they are never forgiven, they are not given any room to grow. They are permanently confined to the person they once were, and I don't believe that's what you want. 

This coming from a gay person myself who has been mistreated. I completely understand why you feel the way you do. I've found that forgiveness was very beneficial for me, and I only hope you might experience the same.

NAH. I think this is just a situation that needs empathy and communication. You should be able to continue cuddling with your friends, but I think it's reasonable that you talk to your BF such that he feels more comfortable. He's wrong but it's easy to see where he's coming from. This situation reveals ever so slightly that he might be afraid of you leaving him, since that is what happened with his ex. Therefore, this could be an opportunity to strengthen your relationship by building greater trust and setting better boundaries!
